correctness.rationale: For three strictly positive masses obeying strict triangle inequalities, vector closure has exactly two conjugate relative-phase solutions. The cyclic angular gaps are pi minus the respective angles of the weight triangle, giving minimum covering arc pi+gamma_min. The actual real projections of the sites span at least this normalized arc but at most |frequency| times support diameter. The equality construction chooses the exact phasor lifts as geometric projections, with a positive transverse height and diameter edge. For independent site differences, all real zeros solve a rank-two modular linear system; its Gram-inverse parametrization and least-norm formula follow by orthogonal decomposition. Rank-one, equal weights, tied smallest weights and nontriangle boundary are explicitly scoped. A standalone seeded checker corroborates selected cases but is not used for infinite claims.

value.rationale: The first real Fourier-zero radius normalized by support diameter is a canonical spectral-geometric invariant. The exact dependence on the smallest angle of the triangle formed by three prescribed masses gives a sharp improvement over the two-phase semicircle bound, distinguishing balanced from near-degenerate mass triples. The theorem is a complete natural three-atom classification, with explicit universally optimal configurations and an exact all-zero lattice for noncollinear sites. No broad general theorem is claimed or needed. The result is not a tabulated computation or a mere rescaling: the mass-angle factor, equality geometry, and rank-two modular structure jointly characterize the invariant.
